result:
Before I write it up, one bigger choice is still open. The recording clean-up was one part. The other is how the whole guide gets built and how volunteers add recordings. Three ways stand out:

1. **Guide pages on your existing website, and volunteers upload to a shared folder.** Each code opens a page on the current site. Volunteers drop recordings into a shared folder, such as Google Drive, with one folder for each exhibit. When the site rebuilds, the recordings are cleaned up and published. Volunteers use a tool they likely know already, and we build almost nothing new. A new recording takes a few minutes to go live. A file in the wrong folder plays at the wrong exhibit.

2. **Guide pages on your existing website, plus a simple upload page.** Volunteers sign in, pick the exhibit and language from a list, and upload. This prevents most mix-ups. It adds sign-in accounts and an upload service to a site that today has no server parts, so there is more to build and maintain.

3. **An off-the-shelf museum guide platform.** Some services host audio guides for museums. There is little to build. Visitors may need to install an app, and the platform may not clean up recordings or support Welsh. I would need to check which ones do.

A dedicated phone app doesn't fit. Visitors would have to install it before they hear anything.

I recommend 1. With sixty exhibits and about ten changes a year, the simplest thing for volunteers to use is worth the small mix-up risk. A check during the clean-up step can flag files with odd names or files in the wrong place.

Which way do you want to go?
